correctness.rationale: Exact normalized Hilbert quotient, equal-weight functional and all quantifiers are fixed. Every two-sample quotient minimizer equals the midpoint of an optimally aligned pair, proved by metric-triangle and Hilbert parallelogram equality. Fourier orthogonality gives exact C_k; for k=2 a cubic on [-1,1] has all maxima classified globally, including equality a=2/5. Fourier mode ratios prove the two above-threshold means inequivalent. For all k, positive phase curvature at zero forces distinct optimal +/- alignments; radial positivity and an explicit smooth planar polar vector field prove embedded hyperbolic-cycle realizability. Exact rational checker identities and numerical quadrature were rerun; finite tests are not the proof. The high-k criterion is sufficient only.

value.rationale: A natural inverse/averaging question for periodic trajectories is whether smooth nearby limit-cycle samples have a unique phase-invariant mean. This establishes its first nontrivial two-lobed embedded family with an exact threshold, complete means/variance, critical quartic degeneracy and square-root branch law; high harmonic perturbations then rule out any C0/L2 uniqueness neighborhood of the reference circle. It identifies concrete failure of a broadly used orbit-averaging functional rather than an arbitrary selected numeric constant or routine corollary.
